transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Um… I guess what finally made me make the appointment is this tension I can’t seem to shake. My shoulders and neck are clenched pretty much all day, like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that just never ends. I know that may sound a little dramatic, but by the evening my jaw aches so much that I can hardly enjoy playing guitar, which is usually something I really look forward to.
Did this tension start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Um… yes, I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like everything comes down to one thing, but it really seemed to start after I was fired from the preschool. That was about a year and two months ago. Since then, the tension’s just kind of… stayed with me.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, even when they’re not related to losing that job?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I try not to let it run away with me, and some of it probably sounds reasonable, but it jumps around a lot. I’ll worry about whether I’ll ever get hired again, and then whether parents think badly of me now, or if I’ve ruined my reputation.

And then it kind of spirals into bigger things, like whether retirement is getting farther out of reach. Sometimes it’s even something small, like if I made a mistake during a story-time activity, my mind turns it into, “Maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with children.” I know that sounds harsh, but that’s where my thoughts go.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worry?

Yes… more than I’d like to admit, honestly. I try to be sensible about it, like I’ll tell myself, “Just make a list,” or “Say a prayer,” or I’ll go outside and weed the garden, or focus on the next practical step.

And sometimes that helps for a minute, but then one worry just sort of hands off to the next one, and before I know it I’ve lost half the afternoon to it. I don’t mean to sound like I’m not trying—I am. It just feels hard to shut off once it starts.
Do your worries mostly center on losing that preschool job?

Mostly, yes… or at least that’s where it starts. I don’t want to overstate it, but my mind doesn’t really stay only on the job itself.

It goes from, “Will I ever get hired again?” to “Have I ruined what parents think of me?” and then to bigger things like whether retirement is slipping farther away. And sometimes it’s embarrassingly small, like if I made one mistake during story time, I start wondering if that means I shouldn’t be trusted with children at all. That sounds awful to say out loud, but… that’s where my head goes.
If you had never been fired from the preschool, do you think this level of tension and worry would still be happening?

I’d like to say no, that it’s just because of being fired… and maybe that is what set it off the most. But I don’t think it would be completely gone.

My mind just keeps circling, you know? It goes from wondering if I’ll ever get hired again, to whether I’ve ruined my reputation with parents, then whether retirement is slipping away. And then I feel silly saying this, but even a small mistake during story time can turn into, “Maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with children anymore.”

I know that may sound like I’m making too much of things… but that’s honestly where my thoughts go.
Has this pattern of tension and hard-to-control worry been present more days than not for at least six months?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been going on since I was fired from the preschool—so, about a year and two months now.

More days than not, yes. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?

I’m not sure, exactly. I mean… I don’t think of myself as a restless person, if that makes sense.

I do feel wound up sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by “keyed up.” I’m not trying to avoid the question—I just don’t want to say yes to something if I’m not describing it right.
Do you often feel tired or easily fatigued?

I don’t know if I’d say “easily fatigued,” exactly. I mean, I do get tired, but I’m 53 and working with little kids is tiring for anyone, right?

So… maybe sometimes, but I haven’t really kept track of it. I don’t want to overstate it.
Aside from the job loss, do you find yourself worrying a lot about things that have nothing to do with being fired?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it mostly connects back to the firing somehow, but it spreads out.

Like, I keep going from “Will anyone ever hire me again?” to “Do all the parents think I’m unsafe or incompetent now?” And then I start thinking about whether I’ve ruined my whole reputation, or whether retirement is slipping away because of this.

And sometimes it gets kind of… unreasonable, I guess. Like I’ll remember some tiny mistake I made during story time and think, “Maybe that means I shouldn’t be trusted with children.” I know that probably sounds extreme. I’m not saying I really believe that all the time, but my mind keeps circling it.
Would you say the main thing bothering you is physical pain?

Not pain exactly… I don’t think of it as, like, a pain condition or anything.

But, honestly, the physical part is kind of what pushed me to come in. My shoulders and neck are clenched almost all day, like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by evening my jaw aches enough that I can barely enjoy playing guitar.

I don’t know if that answers what you mean. It’s not the main “pain” so much as this constant tension.
Even on days when you’re not thinking about being fired, do you still feel anxious or worried?

Yes… I think I do. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m worrying every single second, but even when I’m trying not to think directly about being fired, my mind sort of finds its way back to the same kinds of things.

Like, it’ll go from whether I’ll ever get hired again, to whether I’ve ruined my reputation with parents, or whether this means retirement is going to be harder now. And then sometimes I’ll latch onto something tiny, like a mistake I made during a story-time activity, and think, “What if that means I shouldn’t be trusted with children?” Which… I know sounds like a lot. But yes, it keeps circling.
